footer_tagline: 100% client-side. Your data never leaves your browser.
footer_privacy_text: No server processing. No data collection. No cookies.
viewer_description: View and explore JSON data with a beautiful tree view. Paste your JSON to visualize its structure instantly.
viewer_intro: PureJSON Viewer lets you visualize JSON data in an interactive tree view. Paste your JSON, and instantly see the structure with syntax highlighting. All processing happens in your browser — your data never leaves your device.
viewer_faq_q1: Is my JSON data sent to any server?
viewer_faq_a1: No. PureJSON processes everything 100% client-side using your browser. No data is ever transmitted to any server.
viewer_faq_a2: Yes! PureJSON is a Progressive Web App (PWA). Install it from your browser and use it without an internet connection.
viewer_howto_s1_desc: Paste your JSON into the editor or click 'Open File' to load a JSON file from your device.
viewer_howto_s2_desc: Switch to Tree view to interactively expand and collapse nodes. Hover over values to see their types.
viewer_howto_s3_desc: Use the Code view to edit JSON directly with syntax highlighting, or copy the content to your clipboard.
viewer_feature1: Interactive tree view with expand/collapse for all nodes
viewer_feature2: Syntax highlighting with Monaco Editor (same engine as VS Code)
viewer_feature3: Dual view mode: switch between Code and Tree views instantly
viewer_feature4: Load JSON from file or paste from clipboard — works with large files
viewer_usecase1: Debugging API responses — paste the raw JSON to quickly inspect nested structures
viewer_usecase2: Exploring configuration files — navigate complex config files with the tree view
viewer_usecase3: Validating JSON structure — instantly see if your JSON is well-formed or contains errors
viewer_faq_q3: What is the maximum JSON size supported?
viewer_faq_a3: PureJSON can handle JSON files up to several megabytes, limited only by your browser's memory.
viewer_faq_a4: Yes. If you paste invalid JSON, the editor will highlight syntax errors and the tree view will show an error message indicating the issue.
viewer_faq_q5: Can I edit JSON in the viewer?
viewer_faq_a5: Yes. The Code view provides a full-featured editor with syntax highlighting, auto-completion, and bracket matching. Changes are reflected in the tree view in real time.
formatter_description: Format and beautify JSON with proper indentation. Make your JSON human-readable instantly.
formatter_intro: Beautify your JSON with proper indentation and formatting. Paste minified or messy JSON and get clean, readable output instantly. Choose your preferred indentation level.
minifier_description: Minify JSON by removing whitespace. Reduce JSON file size for production use.
minifier_intro: Compress your JSON by removing all unnecessary whitespace. Reduce file size for faster data transfer and storage optimization.
to_typescript_description: Convert JSON to TypeScript interfaces automatically. Generate type-safe TypeScript types from your JSON data.
to_typescript_intro: Automatically generate TypeScript interfaces from your JSON data. Get type-safe definitions for your API responses, configuration files, or any JSON structure.
to_yaml_description: Convert JSON to YAML format online. Transform your JSON data to clean YAML syntax.
to_yaml_intro: Convert your JSON data to YAML format instantly. YAML is more human-readable and commonly used for configuration files, Kubernetes manifests, and CI/CD pipelines.
tree_invalid_json: Invalid JSON — cannot display tree view
tree_paste_json: Paste JSON to see tree view
confirm_clear_message: Are you sure you want to clear all input and output?
formatter_howto_s1_desc: Paste minified or messy JSON into the input panel on the left.
formatter_howto_s2_desc: Select your preferred indentation style: 2 spaces, 4 spaces, or tab.
formatter_howto_s3_desc: Press the Format button to beautify your JSON. The formatted output appears on the right.
formatter_feature1: Multiple indentation options: 2 spaces, 4 spaces, or tabs
formatter_feature2: Preserves all data values — only whitespace is changed
formatter_feature3: Instant formatting with syntax error detection
formatter_usecase1: Making minified API responses readable for debugging
formatter_usecase2: Standardizing JSON indentation across a team or project
formatter_usecase3: Preparing JSON for documentation or code reviews
formatter_faq_a1: You can choose between 2 spaces, 4 spaces, or 1 tab for indentation. Select your preferred style from the dropdown.
formatter_faq_q2: Does formatting change my JSON data?
formatter_faq_a2: No. Formatting only adds whitespace and indentation. Your data values remain exactly the same.
formatter_faq_a3: No. The formatter requires valid JSON input. If your JSON has syntax errors, an error message will indicate what needs to be fixed.
formatter_faq_a4: There is no hard limit. PureJSON can format large JSON files quickly, limited only by your browser's available memory.
minifier_howto_s1_desc: Paste your formatted or indented JSON into the input panel.
minifier_howto_s2_desc: Press the Minify button to remove all unnecessary whitespace.
minifier_howto_s3_desc: View the size comparison stats showing original size, minified size, and percentage saved.
minifier_feature1: Real-time size comparison with original vs. minified stats
minifier_feature2: Removes all whitespace, newlines, and indentation
minifier_feature3: Preserves all data values — only formatting is removed
minifier_feature4: One-click copy for easy pasting into production code
minifier_usecase1: Reducing JSON payload size for faster API responses
minifier_usecase2: Optimizing JSON configuration files for production deployment
minifier_usecase3: Minimizing localStorage or sessionStorage usage in web apps
minifier_faq_q1: How much space can I save by minifying?
minifier_faq_a1: Savings depend on the original formatting. Typically, you can reduce JSON file size by 20-60% by removing unnecessary whitespace.
minifier_faq_q2: Does minifying change my JSON data?
minifier_faq_a2: No. Minification only removes whitespace. Your data values remain exactly the same.
minifier_faq_q3: Can I minify already minified JSON?
minifier_faq_a3: Yes, but there will be no size reduction since the JSON is already compact. The output will be identical to the input.
minifier_faq_a4: No. Minified JSON is fully valid JSON. It is simply more compact and harder for humans to read, but perfectly parseable by any JSON parser.
to_typescript_howto_s1_desc: Paste a JSON object or array that represents your data structure.
to_typescript_howto_s2_desc: The tool analyzes your JSON and generates TypeScript interfaces automatically.
to_typescript_howto_s3_desc: Copy the generated interfaces and paste them into your TypeScript project.
to_typescript_feature1: Automatic type inference from JSON values (string, number, boolean, null, arrays, objects)
to_typescript_feature2: Nested interface generation for complex object structures
to_typescript_feature3: Array type detection with union types when elements differ
to_typescript_feature4: Optional property detection for keys that may be null
to_typescript_usecase1: Generating types for REST API response payloads
to_typescript_usecase2: Creating interfaces from JSON configuration files
to_typescript_usecase3: Bootstrapping TypeScript types from sample database records
to_typescript_faq_a1: The generator infers types from your JSON values. For best results, provide JSON with representative data so all types are correctly detected.
to_typescript_faq_q2: Can I customize the generated interface names?
to_typescript_faq_a2: The root interface is named RootObject by default. You can rename it after copying the output to your project.
to_typescript_faq_a3: Yes. Each nested object gets its own interface, and the parent interface references it by name. Deeply nested structures are fully supported.
to_typescript_faq_q4: What about arrays with mixed types?
to_typescript_faq_a4: Arrays with mixed element types generate union types. For example, an array containing strings and numbers becomes (string | number)[].
to_yaml_howto_s1_desc: Paste the JSON data you want to convert into the input panel.
to_yaml_howto_s2_desc: The tool converts your JSON to clean, properly indented YAML.
to_yaml_howto_s3_desc: Copy the YAML output and use it in your configuration files, Kubernetes manifests, or CI/CD pipelines.
to_yaml_feature1: Clean, human-readable YAML output with proper indentation
to_yaml_feature2: Handles nested objects, arrays, and all JSON data types
to_yaml_feature3: No reference aliases — each value is written inline for clarity
to_yaml_usecase1: Converting JSON API configs to YAML for Kubernetes deployments
to_yaml_usecase2: Transforming JSON settings into YAML for CI/CD pipeline configuration (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI)
to_yaml_usecase3: Creating YAML-based configuration files from JSON templates
to_yaml_faq_a1: Yes. The converter produces valid YAML that can be used directly in configuration files, Kubernetes manifests, and other YAML-compatible tools.
to_yaml_faq_q2: Does YAML support all JSON data types?
to_yaml_faq_a2: Yes. YAML is a superset of JSON, so all JSON data types (strings, numbers, booleans, null, arrays, objects) are fully supported.
to_yaml_faq_a3: JSON does not support comments, so there are no comments to preserve. The output is pure YAML converted from JSON data.
to_yaml_faq_q4: Can I convert YAML back to JSON?
to_yaml_faq_a4: Not with this tool directly. PureJSON focuses on JSON-to-YAML conversion. However, since YAML is a superset of JSON, you can use a YAML parser to convert back.
to_csv_description: Convert JSON arrays to CSV format online. Transform your JSON data into downloadable CSV spreadsheets.
to_csv_intro: Convert JSON arrays into CSV format instantly. Perfect for importing JSON data into Excel, Google Sheets, or any spreadsheet application.
to_csv_howto_s1_desc: Paste a JSON array of objects into the input panel. Each object will become a CSV row.
to_csv_howto_s2_desc: The tool extracts all unique keys as column headers and converts each object to a row.
to_csv_howto_s3_desc: Copy the CSV output and paste it into Excel, Google Sheets, or save it as a .csv file.
to_csv_feature1: Automatic column header detection from all unique object keys
to_csv_feature2: Proper CSV escaping for commas, quotes, and newlines in values
to_csv_feature3: Handles missing keys gracefully — empty cells for absent fields
to_csv_feature4: Nested objects and arrays are serialized as JSON strings in cells
to_csv_usecase1: Exporting API data to spreadsheets for analysis or reporting
to_csv_usecase2: Converting JSON database exports to CSV for import into other tools
to_csv_usecase3: Creating CSV datasets from JSON log files
to_csv_faq_q1: What JSON structure works best for CSV?
to_csv_faq_a1: An array of objects with consistent keys works best. Each object becomes a row, and each key becomes a column header.
to_csv_faq_a2: Nested objects and arrays are serialized as JSON strings within the CSV cell.
to_csv_faq_q3: What if objects have different keys?
to_csv_faq_a3: All unique keys across all objects are collected as headers. Objects missing a key will have an empty cell for that column.
to_csv_faq_q4: Can I convert a single JSON object (not an array)?
to_csv_faq_a4: Yes. A single object is treated as a one-row table, with keys as headers and values as the single data row.
csv_to_json_description: Convert CSV data to JSON format online. Transform spreadsheet data into structured JSON arrays.
csv_to_json_intro: Convert CSV data into structured JSON arrays instantly. The first row is used as field names, and each subsequent row becomes a JSON object.
csv_to_json_howto_s1_desc: Paste CSV data with a header row into the input panel. The first row defines the field names.
csv_to_json_howto_s2_desc: Each subsequent row is converted to a JSON object using the header values as keys.
csv_to_json_howto_s3_desc: Copy the JSON array output for use in your application, API, or database.
csv_to_json_feature1: Automatic header detection from the first row
csv_to_json_feature2: Proper parsing of quoted fields with commas and newlines
csv_to_json_feature3: Handles escaped double quotes within fields
csv_to_json_feature4: Clean, formatted JSON output with 2-space indentation
csv_to_json_usecase1: Importing spreadsheet data into a web application or API
csv_to_json_usecase2: Converting CSV exports from databases into JSON for frontend use
csv_to_json_usecase3: Transforming CSV log files into structured JSON for analysis
csv_to_json_faq_q1: Does the CSV need a header row?
csv_to_json_faq_a1: Yes. The first row is treated as column headers and used as JSON object keys.
csv_to_json_faq_a2: Yes. Fields enclosed in double quotes are parsed correctly, including fields with commas and newlines.
csv_to_json_faq_q3: Are all values treated as strings?
csv_to_json_faq_a3: Currently, yes. CSV has no type information, so all values are output as strings. You can process them further in your application.
csv_to_json_faq_a4: The tool supports standard comma-separated values (CSV). Tab-separated or semicolon-separated formats are not currently supported.
to_xml_description: Convert JSON to XML format online. Transform your JSON data into well-formed XML documents.
to_xml_intro: Convert your JSON data to well-formed XML instantly. Useful for integrating with XML-based APIs, SOAP services, and legacy systems.
to_xml_howto_s1_desc: Paste the JSON data you want to convert into the input panel.
to_xml_howto_s2_desc: The tool generates well-formed XML with proper indentation and an XML declaration.
to_xml_howto_s3_desc: Copy the XML output for use in SOAP services, legacy systems, or XML-based configurations.
to_xml_feature1: Includes XML declaration with UTF-8 encoding
to_xml_feature3: Nested objects and arrays are converted to nested XML elements
to_xml_feature4: Clean indentation for readable XML output
to_xml_usecase1: Integrating JSON data with SOAP or XML-based web services
to_xml_usecase2: Converting JSON configuration to XML format for legacy systems
to_xml_usecase3: Generating XML documents from JSON data for data exchange
to_xml_faq_a1: Yes. The output includes an XML declaration and properly escaped special characters.
to_xml_faq_q2: How are arrays converted to XML?
to_xml_faq_a2: Each array element is wrapped in a tag using the parent key name, creating repeated sibling elements.
to_xml_faq_q3: What about JSON keys with special characters?
to_xml_faq_a3: Keys containing characters invalid in XML tag names are replaced with underscores to ensure valid XML output.
to_xml_faq_a4: Currently, the root element is named 'root' by default. You can rename it in the output after copying.
sorter_description: Sort JSON object keys alphabetically. Organize your JSON data for better readability and consistency.
sorter_intro: Sort all object keys in your JSON alphabetically. Choose ascending or descending order. Nested objects are sorted recursively.
sorter_howto_s1_desc: Paste the JSON with unsorted keys into the input panel.
sorter_howto_s2_desc: Select ascending (A→Z) or descending (Z→A) from the dropdown.
sorter_howto_s3_desc: All object keys are sorted recursively, including nested objects. Arrays remain in their original order.
sorter_feature1: Recursive sorting — all nested object keys are sorted at every level
sorter_feature3: Preserves array element order — only object keys are reordered
sorter_usecase1: Standardizing JSON key order for consistent version control diffs
sorter_usecase2: Organizing configuration files for better readability
sorter_usecase3: Preparing JSON for comparison — sorting both files before diffing reduces noise
sorter_faq_a1: Yes. Sorting is applied recursively to all nested objects at every level.
sorter_faq_a2: No. Only object keys are sorted. Array element order is preserved.
sorter_faq_a3: No. Only the order of object keys is changed. All values, arrays, and nested structures remain identical.
sorter_faq_a4: Sorted keys make JSON easier to read and compare. They also reduce diff noise in version control, since key order changes won't appear as modifications.
diff_description: Compare two JSON documents and find differences. Highlight added, removed, and changed values.
diff_intro: Compare two JSON documents side by side. Quickly identify added, removed, and changed values with clear path-based output.
diff_howto_s1_desc: Paste the original JSON document into the left panel.
diff_howto_s2_desc: Paste the modified JSON document into the right panel.
diff_howto_s3_desc: The tool compares both documents recursively and shows all differences with their JSON paths.
diff_feature1: Deep recursive comparison of nested objects and arrays
diff_feature2: Path-based output showing exact location of each difference
diff_feature3: Three change types: added (+), removed (-), and changed (~)
diff_feature4: Load JSON from files for easy comparison of large documents
diff_usecase1: Comparing API responses before and after a code change
diff_usecase2: Reviewing configuration file changes between environments (dev, staging, production)
diff_usecase3: Validating data migration results by comparing source and target records
diff_faq_a1: Each difference shows the JSON path, type of change (added, removed, or changed), and the old/new values.
diff_faq_a2: Yes. The comparison is recursive and detects differences at every nesting level, including arrays.
diff_faq_a3: Arrays are compared element by element by index. Added or removed elements at the end are detected, as well as changed values at each position.
diff_faq_q4: What if both JSONs are identical?
diff_faq_a4: If no differences are found, the result will display 'No differences found.' confirming that both documents are identical.
privacy_description: PureJSON privacy policy. Learn how we protect your data with 100% client-side processing.
privacy_section1_p1: PureJSON is built with a privacy-first approach. All JSON processing happens entirely in your browser. No data is ever sent to, stored on, or processed by any server. Your JSON data never leaves your device.
privacy_section1_p2: We believe that developer tools should respect user privacy by default. PureJSON was designed from the ground up to ensure that sensitive data — such as API keys, configuration files, and production data — remains completely under your control.
privacy_section2_p1: PureJSON does not collect, store, or transmit any of the following:
privacy_section2_li1: JSON data you paste, upload, or process in any tool
privacy_section2_li2: Personal information such as your name, email, or IP address
privacy_section2_li3: Usage analytics or behavioral tracking data
privacy_section2_li4: Cookies for tracking purposes (only localStorage for theme/locale preferences)
privacy_section3_p1: PureJSON uses your browser's localStorage to save your theme preference (light/dark mode) and language preference. This data is stored only on your device and is never transmitted to any server.
privacy_section3_p2: You can clear this data at any time by clearing your browser's site data for purejson.org.
privacy_section4_p1: PureJSON uses Google AdSense to display advertisements. Google may use cookies to serve ads based on your prior visits to this or other websites. You can opt out of personalized advertising by visiting Google's Ads Settings.
privacy_section4_p2: No other third-party analytics, tracking, or data collection services are used on this site.
privacy_section5_p1: PureJSON is available as a PWA that can be installed on your device. Once installed, the app works entirely offline. No network requests are made during offline use, further ensuring your data privacy.
privacy_section6_p1: We may update this privacy policy from time to time. Any changes will be posted on this page with an updated revision date. Since PureJSON does not collect user data, policy changes will typically relate to third-party services.
privacy_section7_p1: If you have any questions about this privacy policy, please open an issue on our GitHub repository.

about_description: Learn about PureJSON — free, secure, 100% client-side JSON tools for developers.
about_section1_p1: PureJSON is a free, open-source collection of JSON tools designed for developers, data engineers, and anyone who works with JSON data. Every tool runs 100% in your browser — no server processing, no data collection, no account required.
about_section1_p2: Whether you need to quickly view a large JSON file, format messy API responses, convert JSON to other formats, or compare two documents, PureJSON provides fast, secure, and reliable tools right in your browser.
about_section2_p1: Many online JSON tools send your data to a server for processing. This creates security risks, especially when working with sensitive data like API keys, credentials, or production configurations. PureJSON is different:
about_section2_li1: 100% Client-Side: All processing happens in your browser using JavaScript. No data is ever transmitted to any server.
about_section2_li2: Works Offline: PureJSON is a Progressive Web App (PWA). Install it and use it without an internet connection.
about_section2_li3: Free & Open Source: No subscriptions, no paywalls, no feature restrictions. The source code is available on GitHub.
about_section2_li4: Multi-Language: Available in English, Korean, and Japanese with full localization support.
about_section3_p1: PureJSON offers a comprehensive suite of JSON tools:
about_section3_li1: JSON Viewer & Explorer — Visualize JSON data in an interactive tree view with syntax highlighting
about_section3_li2: JSON Formatter & Beautifier — Format and indent JSON with customizable spacing options
about_section3_li3: JSON Minifier — Compress JSON by removing whitespace to reduce file size
about_section3_li4: Format Converters — Convert JSON to TypeScript, YAML, CSV, XML, and vice versa
about_section3_li5: JSON Diff & Sorter — Compare two JSON documents or sort object keys alphabetically
about_section4_p1: PureJSON is built with modern web technologies: SvelteKit for the framework, Monaco Editor (the same editor used in VS Code) for code editing, and Tailwind CSS for styling. The app is deployed on Cloudflare Pages for global performance.
about_section4_p2: The codebase is written in TypeScript with strict type checking, ensuring reliability and maintainability. All tools are thoroughly tested and optimized for performance, even with large JSON files.
about_section5_p1: PureJSON is open source and welcomes contributions. Visit our GitHub repository to report bugs, suggest features, or contribute code. Together, we can make JSON tools better for everyone.
